about:
JA Electronics Manufacturing Co is based in Stafford, Texas. The company provides custom-engineered cathodic protection solutions for the corrosion prevention industry. While its founding year is not publicly stated, its design team has been advising the cathodic protection sector since 1980. Ownership details and founder names are not disclosed.

The company manufactures air-cooled cathodic protection rectifiers, custom bond boxes and junction boxes, and solar-powered impressed current cathodic protection (ICCP) systems that pair Kyocera photovoltaic panels with its patented Omega II controller. It also supplies anodes (graphite, high-silicon cast iron, platinum/niobium/mixed-metal oxide coated wire), cables, backfill, and field instruments such as holiday detectors, locators, reference electrodes, and thickness testers. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are published.

JA Electronics serves corrosion engineers, field crews, and companies that operate pipelines, tanks, and other metal structures requiring corrosion control. Its training schools travel across the United States, offering hands-on courses in rectifier installation, design methods, maintenance, troubleshooting, and remote communications. Design consulting services are also available for optimizing cathodic protection systems.

The company highlights its Omega II bridge/controller, which delivers up to 50 amperes with 5% or less output ripple—far lower than the 45% ripple typical of standard units—thanks to fold-back voltage and output regulation. Custom enclosures, mounting options, and the ability to engineer solar-powered systems for sites without commercial power are also cited as differentiators.
